maya: PSA: discovered a client-side bug in the sampleapp embedding batcher that produced corrupted vectors during retry merges
kevin: corrupted how?
maya: the merge logic concatenated partial embeddings when a retry returned a different shape, resulting in 1536-length items instead of expected 1024
sam: can you paste the offending snippet?
maya: here it is:
```
// bad merge
function mergeResponses(base, partial) {
  return base.map((b, i) => {
    if (!partial[i]) return b;
    return b.concat(partial[i]); // <- this concat creates longer vectors
  });
}
```
alex: aha. concat assumes segments rather than replacements. Node helper is older; python throws on dim mismatch so parity mismatch here
kevin: two problems: a) merge behavior, b) retries sometimes get routed to fallback model because request grouping headers changed on retry
maya: quick fixes pushed to sampleapp: replaced concat with replace semantics, added dim validation, and a debug flag to log batch ids + shapes. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/pull/812
sam: i'll add CI parity test that injects a mismatched partial response and assert the client errors rather than corrupts data
ci-bot: pipeline triggered: devex/embedding-batcher-parity-check -> started
kevin: docs: add note in onboarding about expected response keys (embedding vs embeddings) and recommend enforcing idempotency headers: x-batch-id + x-request-group
alex: also add changelog entry: "embedding-batcher: stricter merge semantics (breaking)"
maya: follow-ups: add e2e smoke in staging for rerank pages, notify SDK consumers, and backpatch to earlier sampleapp releases if feasible
kevin: assigned: sam (tests), maya (hotfix + docs), alex (changelog). ETA EOD tomorrow
maya: works for me :thumbsup:
